meta.description: The scheduler half of docs/MEMORY_ARCHITECTURE.md §3.3. Orion's audit procedure has always existed in his prompt (app/prompts/agents/orion/02_audit.md) but nothing ever fired it, so passes 1-4 and 6 — boundary sweep, demotion, dedup, compression, audit report — never ran and memory hygiene was nobody's job in practice. This workflow is what makes the custodian a custodian. One turn a night, silent.

nodes.name: Nightly at 04:00
nodes.notes:
04:00 Europe/Istanbul (the workflow timezone below is explicit — do not rely on the container's TZ, which has silently shifted schedules in this system before).

The hour matters: the audit reads the day's session log and recent exchanges, so it must run AFTER the day it is auditing and BEFORE the owner's 08:00 briefings, which read current.md. 04:00 sits in the gap.

Unlike the watch workflows this has no cheap probe in front of it, and that is correct — there is no deterministic question to ask. 'Has memory drifted' is a judgement, and CLAUDE.md's cheap-probe rule says judgement belongs in the turn, not the probe. One turn a night is the whole cost.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ ({"payload": {"type": "cron", "job": "memory_audit", "event": "memory_audit", "automation": "Orion — nightly memory audit", "intent": "Run the current memory custodian procedure. Start and end with memory_audit scan. Review changed documents for subject placement, temporal validity, conflicting records and evidence. Repair narrowly and attest the resulting fingerprints. Report pending review and unresolved defects honestly; never call partial coverage clean."}, "output_mode": "silent"} ) }}

nodes.name: Igor: Orion audit
nodes.notes:
output_mode 'silent' — the audit runs and is stored, nothing is pushed. Orion decides for himself whether the night warrants a notification and sends it from inside the turn (pass 6/7). A push on every no-op night would train the owner to ignore the one night that mattered.

The 10-minute timeout is deliberate: this is a long multi-pass turn walking eight files with the memory tool, not a briefing. Do not lower it to the 20s the briefing workflows use — the turn would be cut off mid-demotion, with a fact removed from its source file and not yet written to its destination.

Retries (3, a minute apart) cover the 503 the trigger returns when the turn registry is at capacity. Missing a night is not catastrophic — the next night's sweep picks up whatever drifted — but retrying is nearly free at 04:00.

TO TEST WITHOUT WAITING: execute the node manually. It costs one real turn and writes real memory changes, so read /memories/.audit/log.md afterwards to see what it did.
